subject: Logging controls & header redaction — follow-up and mutual action items
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Logging controls & header redaction — follow-up and mutual action items

Anna — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary ask: ensure request/response logging does not surface PII (PHI in your case) and that headers (trace IDs, internal cookies) are either redacted or pseudonymized.
- Data residency: logs must remain in the US region and be export-controlled to your security team.
- Retention target: evaluating 30/90/365 day options based on audit needs.

What we committed to deliver by EOD Friday: 
1) short scoping doc outlining how Redwood handles request/response logs and header masking (attached: redwood-log-controls-summary.pdf).
2) examples of configuration toggles (what fields we redact, what we hash).
3) a proposed mutual action plan + dates for a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Ben).

Open questions for you (helps scope the deep-dive):
- Which headers are considered sensitive for Solstice (trace-id, cookie, x-client-id, authorization tokens)?
- Any regulatory minimums on retention for logs we should assume (e.g., 90 days for incident response)?
- Who should Ben loop in from your security/devops for the technical session?

Attachments: redwood-log-controls-summary.pdf (2 pages), proposed-maP.xlsx (MVP action plan).

Thanks — happy to tighten scope once you reply.

—
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Anna Kovacs <anna.kovacs@solsticehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls & header redaction — follow-up and mutual action items

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the attachment. A couple quick answers: 

- Sensitive headers: trace-id and our session cookie (sh_sess) are definitely sensitive. We also consider x-corr-id and any custom x-ssn or x-mrn headers sensitive. Authorization tokens should never be logged.
- Retention: default is 365 days for audit logs, but we can tier to 90 days for higher-frequency logs if needed. 
- Security contact: please include myself and our security lead, Raj Patel (raj.patel@solsticehealth.com). He'll decide whether we need a dedicated VLAN/egress control for log exports.

One more thing: we will need a short proof (screenshot or sample) that the trace-id gets pseudonymized in logs sent to any third-party telemetry. Masking alone is not sufficient for us; we prefer one-way hashing with a salt per-customer.

Can Ben provide an example implementation (pseudo-code or sample config) for trace-id hashing and header redaction?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Kovacs
Senior Security Engineer
Solstice Health
anna.kovacs@solsticehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:20:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls & header redaction — follow-up and mutual action items

Looping in some suggested scoping language Ben can use in the deep-dive. Notes below are for Jordan to send to Anna + Raj before the call so expectations are set.

High-level technical approach (proposal):
- Request/response logging: configurable per-customer toggle. Defaults: log request metadata (method, path, status, latency), do not persist request/response bodies unless explicitly enabled and scoped.
- Header handling: built-in header redaction list (authorization, cookie, set-cookie) + customer-configurable list. For trace-id/x-corr-id we propose two options: 
  a) pseudonymize via HMAC-SHA256 with a per-customer salt (recommended) — reversible only by Redwood if you share the salt (we generally do not).
  b) redact completely (replace with '<REDACTED>').
- Sample retention tiers: 30d (debug), 90d (incidents), 365d (audits). Export controls: logs for dedicated/private customers can be restricted to US regions and delivered to customer-managed S3 with encryption.
- Proofs & demos: Ben can provide a sanitized sample log showing hashed trace-ids and a short snippet of the configuration file that enables header redaction.

Action items for the deep-dive: 
- Ben to demo a live example of HMAC pseudonymization and a simulated export to S3 (30 minutes).
- Security Q&A (Raj + Anna) for policy/contract items (15 minutes).
- If Solstice requires a custom salt rotation policy, we will scope effort and include in the MSA appendix.

Ben — can you prepare the pseudo-code snippet and the sanitized sample logs? Jordan — I'll draft the short scoping paragraph to include in the email to Raj.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

- By Wed 2027-04-28: Technical deep-dive (45m) — Ben (infra), Marissa (product), Jordan (AE), Anna + Raj (Solstice). Proposed slots: Wed 10:00-11:00 or Thu 14:00-15:00 PT. Please confirm.
- By Fri 2027-05-06: Decide retention tiers and export mechanism; Redwood will produce an MSA appendix to cover log handling and salt rotation options.

Attachments: redwood-log-controls-summary.pdf, proposed-maP.xlsx.

If you confirm the timeframe, Ben will also include a short checklist for our security team to validate (S3 encryption, KMS key policy, region lock).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Jordan Blake
